messages.author: 616c278f03e82fc1
messages.subject: differential item functioning
parts:
Hello Dr. Rosseel,

I'm doing DIF test on 9 items related to psychotic symptoms with 2 groups.

Each one of them are 3-cat, so if I want to test whether item i has DIF, I just compare chi square between model with no constraints and model with equal loading and thresholds of item i.
However, my sample size is extremely large, like 4000 in each group, which makes the chi square test over-sensitive, I mean all items have DIF based on it, so do you have any idea how to adjust the significant value (0.05) according to sample size in lavaan.

I also found in some literature that change of CFI could also be used as a criterion, e.g. if change(CFI) < 0.01, then we say this item has no DIF. But this time, in my model all items have change(CFI) < 0.01, then all items have no DIF, which is so contradictory with chi square results, so any clue on how to do adjustment?

I really appreciate your help,
Jinm

I am not sure what you are asking. It is true that p-values depend on
sample size. There is nothing we can do about it. You can choose your
own alpha level. It does not have to be 0.05

This question goes beyond lavaan. You may need consult the literature or
ask elsewhere.

Yves.

messages.author: 7406e44d979f1add
messages.subject: Re: differential item functioning
parts: Global tests are incredibly difficult to calibrate; this is a general problem, not just one of DIF. The only way around it, if you insist on using a global test to verify any assumptions, is choosing a lower significance threshold. A rule of thumb might be along the lines of 5/n or (1-power)/2. Such rules aren't widely discussed in the literature, but prespecifying such a rule and its rationale is acceptable and reproducible. A different approach, with N=4,000, might be to develop a prediction model and calibrate out-of-sample predictive accuracy allowing for fitted values with do and do not allow for DIF.
